notes: One opportunity card per check that warns or fails. lever names a measured sizing lever in audit/sizing.py LEVERS (null: not a revenue lever). category fix_first cards gate the rest: numbers after them are only as good as the fix. Every card is Proposed and its owner UNCONFIRMED until a strategist approves it.

DAT-01.title: Read revenue from the store's live order source
DAT-01.outcome: Every revenue number, flow report and segment reads the store's real orders.
steps: Confirm the store platform with the brand
Pin the live Placed Order metric in Wavy OS
List flows, segments and reports still built on the dormant metric and move them to the live one

readout.metric: Placed Order events on the pinned metric vs the store's order count

DAT-02.title: Re-point flows that listen to dead events
DAT-02.outcome: Flows trigger on events the store still sends.
steps: List live flows whose trigger metric had no events in 90 days
Rebuild each trigger on the live metric
Send a test event and confirm entry

readout.metric: flow entries per week on the re-pointed flows

DAT-03.title: Send line items and one currency with every order
DAT-03.outcome: Product-level flows, cohorts and recommendations have the data they need.
steps: Check the store integration's order payload
Enable line items in the integration settings
Confirm one currency on new orders

readout.metric: share of new orders with line items

DAT-05.title: Complete the account read
DAT-05.outcome: The audit measures every area instead of marking parts unavailable.
steps: Review which reads failed and why
Re-run the audit once the cause is fixed

DAT-06.title: Reconcile attributed revenue with store revenue
DAT-06.outcome: Attributed revenue is reported against the store's own total, so share claims hold up.
steps: Compare Klaviyo attributed revenue to store revenue by month
Note the attribution window and channel split

readout.metric: attributed share of store revenue, month by month

DAT-04.title: Report on the account's own timezone
DAT-04.outcome: Monthly and daily numbers line up with the brand's own books.
steps: Confirm the Klaviyo account timezone matches the store
Re-run month totals on the corrected boundaries

readout.metric: month totals vs the store's month totals

DAT-07.title: Measure sendable reach, not list size
DAT-07.outcome: Planning uses the people who can actually receive email and SMS.
steps: Count consented, deliverable, engaged profiles
Report reach next to list size every month

DLV-05.title: Send from a branded, authenticated domain
DLV-05.outcome: Mail is signed with the brand's own domain, which inbox providers now require for bulk senders.
steps: Set up a branded sending domain in Klaviyo
Publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC records
Verify alignment on a test send

DLV-06.title: Confirm DMARC alignment on live mail
DLV-06.outcome: Live mail passes DMARC, protecting inbox placement at Gmail and Yahoo.
steps: Check received headers on a live send
Fix any SPF/DKIM misalignment

readout.metric: DMARC pass on sampled live sends

CRV-03.title: Fix links that don't reach the live store
CRV-03.outcome: Every click lands on a live, secure page on the current domain.
steps: List links to old domains, failed TLS or wrong destinations
Replace them in the live templates

readout.metric: broken or off-domain links in live templates

CRV-05.title: Make promised offers work at checkout
CRV-05.outcome: Every code an email promises applies at checkout.
steps: List codes in live flows and campaigns
Test each at checkout
Replace expired codes

readout.metric: promised codes that apply at checkout

SMS-05.title: Reconcile the third-party SMS platform
SMS-05.outcome: SMS consent and revenue are counted once across platforms.
steps: Map consent sync between the SMS platform and Klaviyo
Report SMS revenue from one source

FLW-01.title: Build a welcome series for every new subscriber
FLW-01.outcome: New subscribers get a structured first-purchase path.
steps: Map every live form to the list that triggers the welcome
Write 3-4 messages: brand story, hero products, social proof, offer reminder
Exit on purchase

readout.metric: first orders per new subscriber within 30 days

FLW-02.title: Run a full abandoned checkout flow
FLW-02.outcome: Shoppers who start checkout and stop get reminded within the hour.
steps: Trigger on Started Checkout from the live store metric
Send at 1 hour, 1 day and 3 days
Exit on Placed Order

FLW-03.title: Add an added-to-cart flow
FLW-03.outcome: Shoppers who add to cart without starting checkout are followed up.
steps: Confirm Added to Cart events reach Klaviyo
Build a 2-message flow that excludes checkout starters
Exit on Placed Order

FLW-04.title: Add browse abandonment
FLW-04.outcome: Identified shoppers who view products get a relevant follow-up.
steps: Confirm Viewed Product events reach Klaviyo
Build a 2-message flow showing the viewed product
Exclude cart adders and recent buyers

FLW-05.title: Build a post-purchase path to the second order
FLW-05.outcome: First-time buyers get onboarding, usage tips and a next-product suggestion.
steps: Split first-time and repeat buyers
Write thank-you, how-to-use and cross-sell messages
Time the cross-sell before the measured reorder gap

readout.metric: second-order rate of first-time buyers at 60 days

FLW-06.title: Win back lapsed buyers
FLW-06.outcome: Buyers past their expected reorder date get a structured reason to return.
steps: Set entry at 2x the measured reorder gap
Escalate value over 3 messages
Hand non-responders to the sunset flow

readout.metric: reactivated buyers per lapsed buyer reached

FLW-07.title: Sunset unengaged profiles
FLW-07.outcome: Campaigns stop reaching people who never open, protecting inbox placement.
steps: Define unengaged by last open/click and signup age
Send a 2-message re-permission flow
Suppress non-responders

readout.metric: campaign open and spam rates on the engaged audience

FLW-08.title: Raise the flow share of email revenue
FLW-08.outcome: Automated flows earn their share instead of relying on campaigns.
steps: Rank flows by revenue per recipient
Fix the weakest core flow first
Re-check flow share after 60 days

FLW-09.title: Stop flows when the customer buys
FLW-09.outcome: Buyers stop getting abandonment reminders for what they already bought.
steps: Add a Placed Order exit filter to every abandonment and browse flow

readout.metric: abandonment messages sent after a purchase

FLW-10.title: Set flow guardrails
FLW-10.outcome: Smart sending and tracking are on, so flows don't over-send or go unmeasured.
steps: Turn on smart sending for marketing flows
Turn on UTM tracking

CMP-01.title: Set a steady campaign cadence
CMP-01.outcome: A predictable weekly rhythm instead of bursts and gaps.
steps: Agree a weekly send count with the brand
Build a 4-week calendar
Track revenue per recipient by week

readout.metric: campaigns sent per week and revenue per recipient

CMP-02.title: Recover campaign revenue per recipient
CMP-02.outcome: Campaigns earn more per send rather than more sends.
steps: Compare the top and bottom quartile campaigns
Test subject, offer and audience on the next 4 sends

CMP-03.title: Send campaigns to engaged segments
CMP-03.outcome: Campaigns reach people who open, protecting deliverability.
steps: Build engaged 30/60/90 segments
Default campaigns to engaged 90
Expand only for proven sends

readout.metric: campaign open, bounce and spam rates

CMP-04.title: Honour unsubscribes and frequency in every campaign
CMP-04.outcome: Campaign settings respect consent and smart sending.
steps: Audit campaign send options
Turn on smart sending by default

CMP-05.title: Plan peak season against last year
CMP-05.outcome: The peak calendar is built from last year's winners, with no empty weeks.
steps: List last year's peak sends and results
Fill empty peak weeks
Lock the calendar 6 weeks out

DLV-01.title: Cut spam complaints
DLV-01.outcome: Complaint rate stays well under mailbox provider limits.
steps: Find the flows and campaigns with the most complaints
Tighten audiences and fix the worst sources

DLV-02.title: Reduce bounces
DLV-02.outcome: Bad addresses stop dragging down sender reputation.
steps: Find the sources of bounced addresses
Add verification or double opt-in to the worst source

DLV-03.title: Bring unsubscribe rates back to normal
steps: Find the sends with the highest unsubscribe rate
Fix frequency or targeting on those

DLV-04.title: Fix the inbox provider that's falling behind
DLV-04.outcome: Opens at the weak provider recover to the account average.
steps: Send only to engaged profiles at that provider for 2 weeks
Watch opens and bounces there

readout.metric: open rate at the weak provider

RET-01.title: Bring first-time buyers back
RET-01.outcome: More first-time buyers place a second order within a year.
steps: Build or fix the post-purchase path
Time the second-order nudge to the measured reorder gap

RET-02.title: Time follow-ups to when customers reorder
RET-02.outcome: Reorder reminders land just before customers would buy again.
steps: Use the measured reorder gap per product where there's enough data
Move reminder delays to just before it

RET-03.title: Get subscription events into Klaviyo
RET-03.outcome: Subscription starts, renewals and cancellations can drive flows.
steps: Connect the subscription app's Klaviyo integration
Confirm events arrive

RET-04.title: Build subscription lifecycle flows
RET-04.outcome: Subscribers hear before renewals, after failed payments and when they cancel.
steps: Build upcoming-renewal, failed-payment and cancellation flows
Check failed renewals get a message

CAP-01.title: Run a converting sign-up popup
steps: Launch or fix the main popup
Test the offer and timing

CAP-02.title: Grow the list net of unsubscribes
CAP-02.outcome: The email list grows month over month.
steps: Add capture points
Cut the sends driving unsubscribes

CAP-03.title: Connect every live form to a list with a live welcome
CAP-03.outcome: No new subscriber is left without a welcome.
steps: List live forms and their lists
Route each to a list that triggers the welcome

readout.metric: forms routed to a live welcome

CRV-01.title: Keep emails under Gmail's clipping limit
CRV-01.outcome: Gmail shows the whole email, including the unsubscribe link and tracking pixel.
steps: Slim the templates over 102 KB
Re-measure

CRV-02.title: Add live text to image-only emails
CRV-02.outcome: Emails read without images and filter less as spam.
steps: Rebuild image-only templates with live text and alt text

CRV-04.title: Track clicks with UTMs
steps: Turn on UTM tracking for flows and campaigns

SMS-01.title: Collect SMS consent on forms
SMS-01.outcome: SMS reach grows with valid consent. Not for regulated categories (CBD/THC) on Klaviyo SMS.
steps: Confirm the brand's category is allowed on Klaviyo SMS
Add an SMS consent step to the main form

SMS-02.title: Bring SMS messages into compliance
SMS-02.outcome: SMS sends meet quiet hours, opt-out and identification rules.
steps: Fix the flagged SMS settings

SMS-03.title: Lower SMS opt-outs and failures
steps: Find the sends with the most opt-outs
Cut frequency or tighten targeting

SMS-04.title: Make SMS earn its share
SMS-04.outcome: SMS revenue is measurable and growing.
steps: Add SMS to the abandoned checkout flow
Track SMS revenue separately
